newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: Post-election tribal fighting kills 14 in Papua.
newsitem.headline: Post-election tribal fighting kills 14 in Papua.

text.p: At least 14 people have been killed and villages ravaged in post-election violence in Papua New Guinea between highland tribes angry that their candidates failed to win office, police said on Friday.
Losing candidates and their clans have erected road blocks in the mountainous highlands to ambush other tribes and homes have been burnt to the ground.
One tribal fight is now into its fourth week.
"Fighting is just a way of life in the highlands," Chimbu province police commander Allan Kundi told Reuters.
"There has been some election-related fighting. Expectations are high and when people lose in the election they get angry."
Police said eight people had been killed in Chimbu province and six killed in Western Highlands province. Local media reported the post-election death toll in the highlands was at least 20.
"The losing candidates must accept responsibility for all these deaths and destruction of property," said Western Highlands province police chief Titus Pamben.
"They are the only people who can get their people to calm down," Pamben told The National newspaper on Friday.

In Papua New Guinea politics, millions of kina (dollars) are legally spent buying votes at each election and voters expect winning candidates to provide immediate benefits to their remote villages, such as better health care and roads.
In the June election, more than 50 parliamentarians, including 15 government ministers, lost their seats in a voter backlash against political corruption.
